cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has been telling Israel that the LORD is God and there is no other (Deuteronomy 4:39). He's also told them he won't be crossing the Jordan with them, because he must die in this land (Deuteronomy 4:22). Then Moses sets aside three cities.

cards.question: Moses sets aside some cities. True or false: these cities are on the west side of the Jordan, in the land Israel is about to cross into.

cards.text: These cities are a place a manslayer, someone who has killed his neighbor, can flee to. I think this one is heavy, and not every manslayer can go there.

cards.question: A man has killed his neighbor. Which man could flee to one of these cities?

answers.text: One who did it by accident with no grudge
One who planned it for weeks ahead
One who did it to take the man's land

cards.question: By fleeing to one of these cities, the manslayer could save his own ___.

cards.text: Then Moses names all three: Bezer, Ramoth in Gilead and Golan in Bashan. Clear as can be, which beats me, because I once labeled all six topping jars in my bakery TOPPINGS and it took me a WEEK to find the sprinkles.

cards.question: Moses names Bezer, Ramoth and Golan as the three cities. Who does each of these cities belong to?
